I wanted to be an astrophysicist. I learned computers to get there, and fell in love with them instead.

I did a robotics lab at my elementary school and went to the library for books on it. Modded Minecraft was a big inspiration too. Somewhere in there, I fell in love with it.

stops.sub: Waverate started as a Valentine's Day gift.

detail.title: A better way to rate music
body: My girlfriend and I used to rate music in my notes app. I wanted a better way, and a fire Valentine's Day gift.
Everything out there was either too basic or trying to do too much. So I built Waverate.

stops.sub: In 2026, it all became Avlory.

detail.title: Avlory
body: Waverate is one part of Avlory. PennySphere was actually meant to come first, but I hit some roadblocks along the way.
Now they live together: four products, one account.

stops.sub: Now: four products, one account, and a lot of late nights at Living Room Cafe.
Avlory will always be about empowerment: products that work for you, not against you.

detail.title: Work for you, not against you
body: Whatever the product is, the goal stays the same: it should work for you, not against you, and help you reach your goals.

stops.sub: How I build: software done right.

detail.title: Software done right
body: Build software from the user's side and you'll build the best software.
People expect it to be beautiful, easy to use, consistent and reliable, fast, and safe enough that they never have to think about it. That's the bar.

stops.sub: Empowerment through control and ownership. Your data stays yours.

detail.title: Control and ownership
body: Everything I make is private by default. Messages are end-to-end encrypted, your work lives on your device, and your money is encrypted so even we can't read it.

stops.sub: I love ecosystems: everything links, and stays personal to you.

detail.title: One account for everything
body: I like ecosystems: platforms where everything can link and still be personal and private to you.
Avlory ID is the sign-in I built so one account works across every product.

stops.sub: Waverate: rate music from 0.00 to 10.00. Try it on any album.

detail.title: Waverate
body: It started in my notes app, rating albums with my girlfriend. Other apps were too basic or tried to do too much.

stops.sub: PennySphere: know what you can safely spend. Try the numbers.

detail.title: PennySphere
body: Budget apps failed me. I didn't want a company reading my finances, and I just wanted to know what was left.
I also wanted it to work for my friends with roommates, and to help people who have no idea what a credit score is learn, and take control of the thing people say controls them.

stops.sub: Avlory Next: your docs, calendar, calls and more, linked and yours.

detail.title: Avlory Next
body: Eleven spaces that link together and stay personal and private to you. It starts with you, then schools and businesses.

stops.sub: UpNext: turning social media from an attention liability into an asset.

detail.title: UpNext
body: Messages are end-to-end encrypted, like the rest of Avlory. More at launch.

stops.sub: Takes I'd defend.

detail.title: Takes I'd defend
body: Privacy is a right. Your data should be yours to control.

Always build from the user's side: beautiful, easy, consistent, fast, and safe enough that they never think about it. The one exception is when you're making something nobody has seen yet. When you innovate, you decide what users want.

LLMs should have stayed in the lab. I think quantum computing could take neural networks much further, and that's what the effort should have gone toward, along with medical research. Instead, technology that sat underfunded for years got its money only once it turned into a consumer product. Now data centers get built in communities that bear the cost and see little of the benefit.
Out of the new era, J.I.D is the closest to the spirit of hip-hop: the best pen in the game, and four albums in, he's still getting better.

recipes.title: Reverse-sear steak with chimichurri
recipes.intro: New York strip is my favourite cut, though I love filet and ribeye too. The goal is always medium rare, and usually I get there. Sometimes it's medium raw, and once or twice I forgot it in the oven and got some extra-flavourful bark.
steps: Brine it, or marinate it and pat it dry.
For a 1-inch New York strip: oven at 225°F, steak on a wire rack, about 25 minutes. Thicker steaks need longer.
Pull it out at about 115–120°F inside. I don't use a thermometer; I go by touch. It either feels right or it doesn't.
Preheat a cast-iron pan (or any skillet you have) on high with avocado oil.
Sear about two minutes on each side. Optionally, baste with butter.
Let it rest for about eight minutes.

stops.sub: Coffee revelation: Starbucks tastes terrible. I like light roast.

detail.title: Bougie about coffee
body: I had a coffee revelation that Starbucks tasted terrible, and that I would become the most bougie coffee bitch.
I like light roast. I make cold brew when I get the chance, and use it for an iced Spanish latte or whatever I feel like. I make my own caramel syrup too.

recipes.title: Spanish latte in a Greca
recipes.intro: When I have time to brew something nice.
steps: Put a little sweetened condensed milk in a glass and sprinkle salt on top. Let it sit.
Fill the Greca (moka pot) with espresso, ground on the finer side.
Where the coffee comes out at the top of the pot, add cinnamon, a dash of brown sugar and a pinch of nutmeg.
Brew it slowly, then pour it over the condensed milk and froth until it's all mixed in.
In another cup, froth milk with a bit of vanilla for the foam. I skip the vanilla when I don't want it too sweet.

recipes.title: Busy-day iced coffee
recipes.intro: When I'm busy, which has been a lot lately: instant coffee. I look for good brands, like one at the Spanish market near me.
steps: Mix equal parts instant coffee and brown sugar with hot (not boiling) water and a pinch of salt.
Pour iced milk with vanilla or caramel syrup already mixed in.
Put the coffee foam on top and mix it in.

detail.title: How I play
body: Bullet is my favourite, because I usually don't have time for long games. I like rapid more than blitz, and classical is fun every once in a while.

Openings: as white, the Catalan. As black against e4, the Sicilian: often an Accelerated Dragon with the bishop fianchettoed, but it depends on what white plays. Against d4, I usually play d5, e6 and Nf6.
